name: Atmospheric liquid DnB break: 4-bar two-step kick/snare loop with the second kick quieter, kick EQ by dipping mids (not boosting lows/highs), one-shots tightened by shortening decay, a high-passed sliced break and percussive tops grouped and ducked to kick/snare, transient shaper + low-cut on tops, light glue compression into a soft clipper, and a very short no-pre-delay drum room
goal: Build an atmospheric drum & bass drum layer from a kick, a snare, percussive one-shots and a sliced break, so the break adds constant movement without clashing with the kick and snare, and peaks stay controlled for an easy loud master. Delta vs drum clusters: sample/break layering and bus processing (mid-dip kick focus, decay-shortened one-shots, tops ducked to kick/snare, soft-clipped glue bus, tiny drum room) rather than synthesis or pure programming.

source.title: How to make Atmospheric Liquid DNB Drums Step by Step [Beginner Tutorial]

prerequisites: DAW with sampler/one-shot mode or transient warping, slicing, groups
EQ, utility gain automation or sidechain, transient shaper, glue compressor with soft clip, short reverb on a return

inputs.name: samples
inputs.description: Kick, snare, rim/perc one-shots, shaker, a breakbeat loop

outputs.name: dnb_drums
outputs.description: Balanced atmospheric DnB drum loop at ~170-175 BPM

constraints: Original synthesis/processing recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any DAW/synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks, impulse responses or samples copied.
Processing is contextual: revisit it once the rest of the track exists.
Use original or licensed samples; no sample pack contents copied.
Drums early (Matt's taste): if the track has drums, the kick/drum loop enters by about count 8 (roughly 10-12 s), with only the pad before that.

steps.action: Program a 4-bar two-step kick/snare loop; lower the second kick in each bar slightly so beat 1 is the strongest hit.
EQ the kick by dipping the mids (focuses the low and top without boosting), tame its top a little, and cut any low noise bump.
Tighten percussive one-shots and the shaker by pitching where useful and shortening their decay (one-shot/gate mode), since reverb is added later.
Bring in a break: tighten its decay, slice it, rearrange slices to fit the kick/snare rhythm, and high-pass it so it only adds top-end movement.
steps.expect: Constant rhythm over the main hits

steps.action: Group all top elements (break, percs, shaker). Duck the group on kick and snare (utility gain automation or sidechain) so tops never clash with the focal transients.
On the tops group: a transient shaper, then an EQ that removes any low bleed and rolls off harsh highs.
Drum bus: glue compressor with light compression and soft clip on, driving into the clipper so no spiky transient peaks too hard; then balance kick, snare and tops (levels change the compression).
steps.expect: Even peaks, easy to master loud

steps.action: Send to a very short drum-room reverb with no pre-delay and short decay.
steps.expect: Drums gain life without long tails masking them

verification: Beat 1 kick is louder than the second kick.
Tops are audibly ducked on kick and snare hits.
No transient spikes above the clipper ceiling.
Reverb tail is short enough that hits stay distinct.
